agents.report:
I've researched TJX, Ross and Burlington to the point where new searches mostly repeat what I'd already found. These items are still missing:
- the TJX call transcript and Q&A (not posted yet)
- named analyst reactions to TJX's report
- live prices for ROST and BURL today
- current Burlington and Ross consensus (sources disagree, details below)

## Summary
TJX's beat was a "less bad than feared" result, and the market took it as a relief that Marmaxx is stabilizing. The setup for the next sessions is Ross and Burlington reporting into a sympathy bounce. The two companies are very different: Ross has strong data but a high bar, and Burlington has a lowered bar but weak trends.

## TJX (reported this morning before the open)
**The quarter** ([TJX 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm)):
- Net sales were $15.95B, up 6%. Consolidated comp was +4% against a company plan of 2-3% and a consensus of about 2.9-3.8% (sources differ).
- Adjusted EPS was $1.34, in line with consensus. Reported EPS was $1.39, including a $0.05 net tariff-refund benefit.
- Marmaxx (TJ Maxx, Marshalls) comp was +2%. That is up from +1% in Q2 but down from +6% a year ago. Segment profit was down, at a 13.8% adjusted margin.
- Other segment comps: HomeGoods +5%, Canada +6%, International +8%.
- Adjusted pretax margin was 12.5%, down 0.2 points. Adjusted gross margin was down 0.5 points on freight and fuel.
- Inventory per store was flat. Management called marketplace availability "outstanding", which is good for buying.

**Guidance:**
- Q4 comp is guided to +2-3%. Q4 adjusted EPS is guided to $1.42-1.45, below the roughly $1.48 estimate cited ([Futu](https://news.futunn.com/en/post/1004908999/shares-of-tjx-tjxus-the-leader-in-discount-retail-surged), [Blockonomi](https://blockonomi.com/tjx-companies-tjx-stock-jumps-7-as-holiday-outlook-backs-q3-beat)).
- Full-year comp was raised to +4%. Full-year adjusted EPS is $5.17-5.20 (the low end was raised from $5.15). That sits below the roughly $5.23-5.25 the Street wanted.
- The buyback is now about $3.0B, and the dividend was raised to $0.48 from $0.425.
- Q4 absorbs extra fuel costs and tariff-related bonus accruals, and no more refunds are expected.
- Management said warm weather is "holding back" some categories, but expects momentum to accelerate through the holidays and Marmaxx to improve further in Q4.

**Why it jumped:**
- The stock was near its 52-week low (prior close $129.85, low $122.78, high about $170 earlier in 2026). Estimates and targets had been cut this month: Gordon Haskett downgraded to hold on Nov 13, and Morgan Stanley, UBS, Wells Fargo and Baird cut targets ([Investing.com preview](https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/tjx-faces-earnings-test-as-offprice-model-meets-margin-pressure-93CH-5033365)).
- UBS had expected Marmaxx at +1%.
- Pre-market was +5.5% to 6%. It traded at about $139.42 mid-morning ([Blockonomi](https://blockonomi.com/tjx-companies-tjx-stock-jumps-7-as-holiday-outlook-backs-q3-beat)). That was on pace for its biggest one-day gain since Aug 2024.
- [StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/tjx/news/earnings/tjx-exceeds-q3-cy2026-expectations-stock-soars) called it a mixed quarter with a softer outlook. The rally was driven by relief and positioning, not a clean beat.
- Target's comp of +5.6% (against about 3.8% expected) came out the same morning, a sector-friendly backdrop ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/stocks/macro-signals-from-today-s-earnings-target-tjx-and-lowe-s)).

**The Marmaxx story:** In August, Marmaxx comp slid to +1% from +6% the quarter before. Herrman called it "self-inflicted", saying apparel assortments reached stores late. TJX fell about 4% that day ([Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/22/ross-stores-grew-comparable-sales-10-tjx-grew-4-only-one-stock-went-up/)). The +2% is a modest recovery, not a full one. Placer.ai foot traffic shows T.J. Maxx turning positive in September and accelerating in October, while Marshalls same-store visits were flat ([Placer.ai](https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/off-price-on-course-ross-and-tjx-in-q3-2026)).

## Ross (reports Thursday Nov 19, after the close, call 4:15 PM ET)
Ross is the strongest operator of the three, and the bar is high.
- **Q2 (August):** Comp was +10% on top of +2%. EPS was $2.66 against guidance of $1.85-1.93, including about $0.60 of tariff refunds ([Ross 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000745732/000074573226000038/q226exhibit991.htm)). Excluding refunds, operating margin was up 205 bps against a plan of 130-150 bps. The stock rose about 4% the next day.
- **Guidance:** Q3 comp is guided +6-7% and EPS $1.75-1.83. Q4 comp is guided +4-5% and EPS $2.17-2.26. Full-year EPS is $8.61-8.77. Inventory was up 18% against sales up 13%.
- **Expectations:** Consensus is about 7% comp and EPS $1.82-1.93 (sources differ). StreetSignal's checks point to roughly 10% comp and a $1.93 EPS bogey ([StreetSignal](https://streetsignal.substack.com/p/ross-stores-eps-bogeys)). That means the real bar is above guidance.
- **Data:** Placer.ai shows Ross same-store visits up 12.3% in Q3, with every month near or above +10% ([Placer.ai](https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/off-price-on-course-ross-and-tjx-in-q3-2026)).
- **Analysts:** Deutsche Bank (Nov 13) raised its Ross comp estimate to 9% from 7% and prefers Ross and TJX ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/deutsche-bank-favours-ross-stores-and-tjx-for-earnings-upside-into-2027-5026517)). UBS upgraded to Buy on Oct 26 with a $315 target and calls Q3 "very solid", but notes expectations are priced in. The last close cited was about $220, and the average target is about $273 ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/ross-stores-likely-to-deliver-very-solid-q3-ubs-says-ce785ed8d088f026)).
- **Valuation and positioning:** Ross trades at roughly 26x FY27 earnings. It was up about 27% YTD before today, while TJX was down 8.5% and Burlington down 17.8%. The risks are a strong-but-priced-in quarter, a Q4 guide that is merely fine, and tougher 2027 comparisons.

## Burlington (reports Tuesday Nov 24, before the open, call 8:30 AM ET)
That is the 4th session from now (Nov 19, 20, 23, 24), so it falls inside a 1-10 session hold. Burlington is the weakest story of the three, which fits the screen showing only one of the three above its 50-day average.
- **Q2 (Aug 27):** Sales were $3.00B, a small miss against about $3.02-3.03B. Adjusted EPS was $2.37 against $2.17 expected. The stock fell 6-8% on the day; sources differ on the exact figure ([Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/31/burlington-burl-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
- **Guidance:** Q3 comp is guided +1-3% and adjusted EPS $1.60-1.70. About $55M of tariff refunds is being reinvested in lower prices (about 40% in Q3, 60% in Q4), which cuts Q3 operating margin by 60-80 bps. Management flagged:
  - a consumer squeezed by high gas prices
  - a possible "super El Niño" hurting outerwear
  - 1.5 points of comp cannibalization from new stores
  - competitors possibly matching its price cuts
- **Estimates:** MarketBeat shows consensus of about $1.72-1.73 EPS on about $2.97-2.99B of sales (the consensus figures vary by source, and a stale $2.04 EPS figure also circulates). Deutsche Bank cut its comp estimate to 2% from 4% on softer trends and weather.
- **Price:** About $254-257 around Nov 9-10, down about 33% over 3 months, with a 52-week low near $227. Cantor was neutral on Nov 10 with a $270 target, and the average target is about $350.
- **Options:** The options market implies a move of about 9% on earnings. BURL's last eight earnings-day moves ranged from -14.1% to +6.5%, with three of the last four negative ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/burlington-stores-stock-may-swing-9-on-nov-24-earnings-report-93CH-5033525)). The Aug 27 move there is listed at -14.1%, which conflicts with the 6-8% decline in other sources.
- **Read-through:** Burlington is the least affected by TJX's results (TJX's apparel-heavy Marmaxx is the closest comparable, and it only inched up). If Burlington moves with the basket today, that is sympathy, not new information.

## Sector and macro backdrop
- **Diesel and freight:** Bank of America (October) cut estimates and targets on all three, keeping Buy ratings. It cites diesel at about $6.35 a gallon (about 73% above a year ago, after the Iran war) and says trucking contracts renew in April, a risk that has not hit margins yet. It put Burlington's target at $344 and the combined hit at about $595M ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/node/62633232)). TJX has now put extra fuel cost into its Q4 guide.
- **Tariff refunds:** The Supreme Court ruled IEEPA tariffs unlawful on Feb 20, 2026. Customs began paying refunds through a portal that opened April 20. Refunds inflated Q2 and Q3 results for all three (TJX $463M over nine months, Ross $253M in Q2). Clean comparisons are noisy, and there are no more refunds in Q4 ([NRF](https://nrf.com/blog/ieepa-tariff-refunds-are-moving-forward)).
- **Consumer:** The theme is trade-down and value, with the lower-income shopper stretched. Warm weather is hurting seasonal categories, and holiday forecasts are about +5% (Deloitte). I could not confirm anything about Walmart's November 2026 report or what has driven XRT lower over 20 sessions.

## Takeaways for a 1-10 session decision
1. **TJX:** The catalyst is spent, and today's +8% is the gap. It closed at $129.85 and is near its lows, so the move erases weeks of declines. Q4 guide, fuel and the warm weather are the open issues. I'd treat further upside as dependent on Ross's print.
2. **Ross:** Tomorrow after the close is a binary event with a high bar (the real expectation is about 9-10% comp and EPS near $1.93). The data is the best of the group, but the stock may already be pricing it in, and today's sympathy bounce adds to that.
3. **Burlington:** The Nov 24 report is inside the window. Expected move is about 9%, trend is weak, and the stock rallied today on the basket. Burlington has the worst fundamentals but the lowest bar, so the print could cut either way.
4. **Basket:** The basket's +3.5% today is mostly TJX (+8.1%), so it is not a broad signal. Over the next sessions the main variables are Ross's comp against 9-10%, and whether Marmaxx's improvement holds.

agents.report:
Searches had mostly stopped surfacing new facts by this point. I did not find any GDX-specific news for today. The story is a gold and silver rout driven by Fed hike expectations.

## GDX thesis summary (as of 8:55 AM CT, Wed 2026-11-18)

**What is driving today's drop**
- Spot gold is down about 2.1% to 2.4%, near $3,770. It touched $3,757, the lowest since September 2025. Spot silver is down about 3.4% to roughly $45.8, and platinum is down 3.4%. This matches your screen: SLV and GLD are breaking their lows too.
- GDX is falling about 5.7%, roughly 2.5 times gold's move. That is the usual operating leverage of the miners.
- The cause is macro, not anything specific to GDX:
  - The dollar is near a 19-month high.
  - The 10-year Treasury yield is around 5%.
  - The Fed raised rates in September, its first hike since 2023.
  - CME FedWatch shows about a 95% to 97% chance of a 25 bp hike at the December 8-9 meeting.
  - New York Fed President Williams said more hikes are likely.
  - St. Louis Fed President Musalem said several more may be needed.
  - A Bybit analyst described the market as pricing about three more hikes through mid-2027.
- Oil and inflation tied to the Iran conflict are feeding the hawkish Fed. Gold is not acting as a safe haven in this episode.

**The larger arc**
- Gold peaked near $5,600 and silver near $121.65 in January. Both then crashed, with Venezuela and Iran tensions and the Warsh Fed pick cited as triggers.
- Gold is now about 32% below its peak and silver about 62% below. Gold is down over 10% for the year, on track for its worst year since 2015.
- GDX's 52-week range of 69.74 to 117.18 fits this arc. It is still roughly 8% above its 52-week low.
- GDX closed at 78.95 on Nov 16, down 3.3% that day.
- VanEck data show GDX's NAV was about $79 on Nov 2 and $86.86 on Nov 10. The fund bounced early in the month and is now giving the bounce back. Your 50-day average of 86.99 sits near that bounce level.
- Gold's realized volatility is about 29% this year, about twice its five-year norm. Year to date through Oct 31, gold was down 10.3%, GDX down 10.1% and GDXJ down 16.5%.

**Miner fundamentals**
- Q3 results were fine, but guidance was a drag.
  - Agnico Eagle beat earnings at $2.62 a share. It guided full-year output to the low end and costs to the high end. Diesel is adding about $30 an ounce now and possibly $50 to $60 in Q4. The stock fell about 3% on the results.
  - Newmont's Q3 all-in sustaining cost was $1,454 an ounce, with free cash flow of about $1.9B. A single, less established source says Q4 costs rise toward $1,900 an ounce. The stock fell 4.4%.
- Margins are still large at $3,770 gold against costs of roughly $1,500 to $1,650. The pressure is on the price of gold and on cost inflation, not on solvency.

**Support for gold, and the bull case**
- Central banks bought 675 tonnes of gold from January to September, 6% more than a year earlier.
- Gold ETFs added 211 tonnes in Q3.
- UBS calls the sell-off positioning-led, not structural. ANZ sees support near $3,600.
- Goldman Sachs cut its year-end target to $4,150, and a headline on the Kitco page says it expects $5,600 again in 2028.
- One technical writer sees gold support at $3,707 (61.8% retracement), then $3,628. Another source gives $3,450. The same technical writer is bearish on the daily and weekly charts.

**Catalyst today and flow context**
- The minutes of the Oct 27-28 Fed meeting come out at 2:00 PM ET, which is 1:00 PM CT, today. With a hike already priced in, the question is how split the committee was and whether the minutes imply hikes into 2027.
  - A split committee could trigger a relief bounce in gold.
  - A broad hawkish consensus would extend the drop.
  - This falls after your 8:55 AM CT entry window and inside the one-to-ten-session horizon, so it is the main event risk for any trade.
- Other things to watch: oil prices (North Sea Dated crude fell from $136 in early October to about $93), the dollar and yields, and the December Fed decision.
- GDX has seen large outflows over the past year (about $3B net per Investing.com), and net assets were about $26.9B on Nov 6. I found no dated outflow figures for this week.
- I found no CFTC positioning data and no current GDX options data.

**Takeaways for the trade decision**
- The selling is macro and rates-driven, and it is broad across metals. Technically the trend is down (50-day below 200-day, new lows across GDX, SLV and GLD).
- A bounce would likely come from a dovish surprise in the minutes, an oil or dollar pullback, or oversold mean reversion from a 1.3 ATR gap down.
- The bear continuation case is hikes priced further into 2027, with gold falling toward $3,600 or lower. A GDX move through its 52-week low of 69.74 would need gold to fall a further 5% to 8%.
- The $3,600 to $3,630 gold zone and GDX's 69.74 low are the nearest reference levels.

**Reliability caveats**
- The searches returned some inconsistent dates (for example, labeling Nov 17 a Wednesday). I used the figures that were consistent across the Kitco/Reuters, Deccan Chronicle and Yahoo/Euronews pieces.
- The Newmont Q4 cost figure and the figures for Barrick are weakly sourced.
